title: Add up what you can
description:
A file of measurements has been damaged: some entries are numbers and some are junk. Read entries separated by spaces or new lines until the input ends. Add up the whole numbers, count the entries you had to skip, and print:

```
Sum: 20
Skipped: 2
```

(for the input `4 x 10 abc 6`).

Reading stops when there is nothing left. A read can fail for two reasons, and you must tell them apart:

- the input ran out: `std::cin.eof()` is true, so stop;
- the next entry is not a number: clear the error, read the junk into a `std::string` to remove it, count it, carry on.
hints: After a failed read, check `std::cin.eof()` **before** calling `clear()`. If the input has simply run out, leave the loop.
To remove one junk entry: `std::cin.clear();` then `std::string junk{}; std::cin >> junk;`
